resources.string: The thin liquid film covers the exposed surface and helps smooth the first optical interface.
Several layers of epithelial cells cover the front of the cornea, beneath the tear film.
A thin, dense layer lies between the epithelium and the main stroma.
Organized collagen sheets make up most of the thickness. Layer thickness in this drawing is exaggerated for clarity.
The basement membrane of the endothelium lies at the back of the stroma.
A single layer of cells faces the aqueous humor and helps regulate fluid in the cornea.
Fluid in the anterior chamber contacts the inner surface of the cornea.
A clear capsule envelopes the lens and provides a surface for zonular attachments.
The epithelial layer is on the anterior side just inside the capsule. It is not continuous across the back surface.
Outer fiber layers surround the central nucleus.
The central region contains older lens fibers. It is not a cellular nucleus.
Suspensory fibers between the ciliary body and lens capsule transmit tension to the lens.
The diagram shows projections of the ciliary body and their position beside the lens equator.
